newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended softer on Monday as investors nervously awaited U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday * Canada unit finished around C$1.3792 (US$0.7250) from Friday's close at C$1.3783 (US$0.7255) * Currency seen trading quietly within narrow range overnight * Bank of Canada seen holding Canada rates steady in face of U.S. rate increase.
Traders did not expect the Canadian dollar to take a huge hit on Tuesday if the Bank of Canada kept Canadian rates steady in the face of a U.S. rate increase.
Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said last week that the central bank had more room to maneuver in reaction to possible U.S. interest rate hikes.
"People are definitely thinking that the Bank of Canada will keep things steady," the trader said.
Some Canadian economists said the Bank of Canada's independence had already been priced into the Canadian dollar, noting the unit last week fell to its lowest point in a year.

"If the bank holds tight, even though the Fed hikes, the Canadian dollar will probably fare much better that it did in 1994-95 after the Mexican peso crisis," said Bank of Nova Scotia economist Mark Levesque.

However, a minority of analysts noted Canada's economy has shown signs of stronger growth which might warrant a small rate increase to spare the Canadian dollar the consequences of resisting a Fed hike.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slipped to 1.2242 marks from 1.2277 marks on Friday and jumped to 89.14 yen from Friday's 88.98 yen.
